message.reasoning:
Let me analyze this week's source packet to identify meaningful evidence moments for wedding-business owners.

I need to look for:
- Meaningful decisions, objections, buyer tensions, process trade-offs, result stories with boundaries, credible observations and teaching mechanisms
- Passages that reveal how a consequential choice works
- Not routine account troubleshooting unless reader-level significance is clear

Let me review the meetings:

**m1** - Carmen & Shannon (Love Like Wild, wedding photographer in Orlando):
- Ad copy review - "no posing" vs "candid moments" tension (Shannon does 90% candids but does help with posing)
- Budget discussion: $500/month starting, $500-750 ideal
- Expectations: first 2 weeks don't touch, 3 days monitoring, 1 month for leads, 3 months to know if truly working
- Negative keywords discussion
- Microsoft Clarity suggestion (free heat map)
- Location targeting: Florida, exclude Panhandle/Tallahassee, target Orlando/Tampa/Sarasota with 10-20% bid increase
- Landing page pop-up discussion
- Videography add-on decision (not advertised as solo)

**m2** - Carmen & Fallon (internal training):
- Process: VIP day takes 2-3 hours now vs 6 hours before
- Tracking setup walkthrough (Google Tag Manager, conversion tracking)
- Client already running Google Ads with zero conversions bidding on wrong keywords (camcorder rental people)
- Expectations messaging to clients

**m3** - Carmen & Shannon (strategy call):
- Budget $500/month
- Search campaign explanation (high intent)
- Maximize clicks → maximize conversions strategy
- Separate landing pages for Orlando vs Denver (different vibes)
- Negative keywords: cheap, affordable, free, DIY, how-to
- Cost per lead issue on Meta (skyrocketed)
- Light and airy photographer misalignment - 1 out of 4-5 became client
- Anti-barn wedding positioning

**m4** - Carmen & Fallon (internal):
- Full-service client on Google Ads for over a year, never performed well - at a loss
- Landing page clarity issue: destination wedding planner + travel agent, vague above the fold
- 20% of people go from page to inquiry form but don't inquire - looking for more info
- Meta ads doing better ($8/day, 11 leads, $21 cost per lead)
- Landing page hero needs to summarize what they do
- Lead volume okay but tours canceling at high rate (55%)
- Cost per lead benchmarks: DJ Hybrid normally $30-50 on Google, now $126
- Dos Palomas: 40% of people going to pricing page view
- Client handover process discussion

**m5** - Carmen & Jillian (waxing business - non-wedding, but shows Google Ads mechanics):
- Cost per booked appointment doubled from $40 to $80
- 6 booked appointments in last 30 days but client says she hasn't had 6 new clients - repeat bookings vs new clients
- Sponsored ads may be helping indirectly (people see ad twice, book organically)
- People scrolling and clicking organic listing instead of ad
- Meta suggested for newer leads, Google for retargeting/fueling
- Duplicate campaign and switch back to maximize clicks test
- Landing page feedback from Jacqueline suggested
- Search terms review - relevant traffic

**m6** - Whitney & Gisselle (internal operations):
- Invoice/payment process issues (ACH, Venmo, PayPal)
- Zoom storage cleanup
- Pricing guide creation workflow (Giselle does first draft, Tina reviews)
- AI chat widget follow-up

**m7** - Whitney team meeting (LeadLock/Foolproof Follow-Up Advantage):
- Competitors Hitched and Nurture Pro lock down workflows; clients moving over
- Email sequences too long, need bite-sized
- Text messages underutilized - venues getting responses in texts not emails
- Post-tour surveys, reactivation workflows, Google reviews inconsistently used
- Non-event workflows pricing clarity needed
- Pricing guide requests increasing

**m8** - Whitney & Fallon & Lauren (The Penny, venue):
- Messaging/positioning interview
- Ideal client: Cal Poly nostalgia, 80-85% out-of-town, tech workers from LA/Bay Area
- All-inclusive vs venue-rental-only comparison confusion ($10k vs $30k)
- Space concern: max 125 seated, intimate weddings fit better
- Accommodations: 2-3 hotels within 2 blocks, Airbnb lofts
- Comparison chart exists on website but not prominent
- Three-layer ad approach (cold attraction, conversion, retargeting) with different creatives
- Booking story behind name (wishing well, pennies)

**m9** - Whitney & Zadie (LeadLock demo, UK wedding photographer):
- Cost objection: $12.97 setup, $147/month vs £20/month for Studio Ninja
- Small business (20 weddings/year) - ROI concern
- Multi-channel lead capture problem (Instagram DMs, TikTok, wedding fairs, website form)
- Manual lead entry defeats purpose
- Dashboard showing funnel conversion rates
- WhatsApp common in UK vs US

Now let me select the most meaningful moments for wedding-business owners. I should focus on:
1. Consequential choices with explained mechanisms
2. Buyer tensions and objections
3. Process trade-offs
4. Credible observations with boundaries

Let me pick the strongest ones:

1. **Google Ads expectations timeline** (m1) - The "don't touch for 2 weeks, 3 days monitoring, 1 month for leads, 3 months to know" framework. This is a consequential expectation-setting decision with clear boundaries.

2. **Ad copy tension: "no posing" vs "candid"** (m1/m3) - Shannon's business is 90% candids but she does help with posing. The copy "no posing" misrepresents. This reveals how ad copy can create false expectations that hurt conversion.

3. **Budget starting point $500** (m1/m3) - Lower budget = less emotional investment, clients don't demand immediate results. Consequential trade-off.

4. **Landing page clarity for destination wedding planner** (m4) - 20% of visitors reach the form but don't inquire because they're looking for more info. Hero section needs to summarize what they do. This is a concrete conversion mechanism.

5. **Meta vs Google for new vs returning clients** (m5) - Google retargeting fuels repeat bookings; Meta gets new leads. Different channels serve different funnel stages.

6. **Cost per lead doubling $40→$80** (m5) - With boundary: client says 6 booked appointments but only ~1-2 were new clients, rest were repeat. Shows attribution ambiguity.

7. **Negative keywords for price-sensitive searchers** (m3) - Excluding cheap/affordable/free because clients with $1,000 budget vs $4,000 starting price waste both parties' time.

8. **Text messages vs emails for venue follow-up** (m7) - Venues getting responses in texts, not emails. Underutilized channel.

9. **All-inclusive vs venue-rental comparison confusion** (m8) - $10k venue rental vs $30k all-inclusive - couples don't understand value because they only see the rental fee. Comparison chart exists but not prominent.

10. **Separate landing pages for different markets** (m3) - Orlando vs Denver need different imagery (mountains vs beach).

11. **Microsoft Clarity free heat map** (m1) - For quality ads but no leads, shows what's happening on site.

12. **Small business cost objection** (m9) - $147/month vs £20/month, 20 weddings/year. Shows pricing tension for smaller businesses.

13. **Multi-channel lead capture problem** (m9) - Instagram DMs, TikTok, wedding fairs all need manual entry, defeating automation.

14. **Landing page feedback loop** (m5) - Getting Jacqueline's feedback on landing page to improve conversion rate.

15. **Expectations messaging to avoid client panic** (m2) - Clients freaking out if no leads immediately.
